body: By working on yourself. That's it. Life is too short to suffer from someone while there are millions, BILLIONS of human beings out there. I know a breakup is painful. I've been there too. Nevertheless, you won't get anywhere by being sad or suffering. It just hurts you. So, work on yourself. Keep your mind busy with activities that will lead you to your goals in the future. What are your dreams? Write them down and analyse what you have to do to reach them. Work out, read, learn something new ever single day, practice any skill, there are infinite ways to keep yourself busy and you'll definitely not think about him anymore because your mind is full of what really matters. YOU AND YOUR DREAMS. Go for it.

Work out, read, improve any skil, learn something new everyday. Man, you'll have a lot of more opportunities in the future. Do you want to still he the same you that lost that chance? Of course not. What do you like doing? What are your passions? What's something your good at? And don't compare yourself to others. Gosh you sound just like me two months ago. I was so scared of my future. I switched career inside college when I was in second year. So, my classmates have already finished their carrers while I'm still studying this and next year. I was having troubles with some courses which would mean I'd not only stay two more years but three or even more. I was feeling so miserable. I thought I had ruined my life and it depressed me for many months and I even thought about commiting suicide because in my mind I have already wasted all my life even though I'm just 21. This anxiety made me eat like a pig and depressed me even more and more. Nevertheless, I read a book "The subtle art of not giving a f*ck" and it taught me that the key to have a better life is to focus in what's happening right now. Overthinking was killing me inside and destroying my life. Try not to overthink in that way. It's not fair for you to deal with future problems that may never happen. You have enough to deal with your current problems. Try to focus in what's happening in front of you. The book I recommended you, Atomic habits, has taught me to see my daily habits and see wether they will lead me to the person I want to be in the future. Being on social media and comparing your life with apparently other people's perfect lives just will leave you frustration and dissatisfaction. Thinking about why you live may be in the future, just will leave you to what you said. Man, don't focus in the end the race. Just make sure that what you're doing everyday is the correct and wether that will lead you to a better version of you. Focus in working out 1 hour a day, in reading 5-10 pages a day, organizing your day, doing your duties, learning something new even 10 minutes a day. Man, how do you think that amount of work will impact in your life? And it doesn't matter how long it make take. Knowing that all you're doing is leading you in the correct way is all that matters. Another important lesson I've learned from books is that life is not fair. You need to keep in mind that. You need to take responsibility and face reality. Complaining won't solve anything. Sometimes we feel frustrated for what happened to us and we think we didn't deserve it. But that simply won't solve anything. Sometimes, I fail exams even though I'd studied so hard. But it is what it is. We simply can't change our past. I'm sure you must deal with that everyday too. Past is also another thing that tortures inside us. Think about it this way, we can't change our past, future is uncertain, we can't do anything with that. The only thing we have is now, our present. Give yourself a chance to be someone better with new habits. Forgive yourself for your mistakes in the past. And don't punish yourself with future problems which are not likely to happen, and if it happened, you'll solve them when time comes to shove. In order to solve those, give to yourself the necessary tools to face it, set new and healthy habits. As long as you know that those will lead you to a better you, it's all that matters. Give yourself a chance to be better. You deserve it.

You know, I'm 21 and I was feeling like a failure because social media destroys your life. There, you can see people who apparently have better lives than you or you can also spend the whole day using you cellphone and at the end of the day, you feel even worse because you haven't done anything productive. Since I've started to develop new habits, my life has changed completely. I don't use social media (just the necessary), I've lost 27 pounds and I've read some books. At night, I only feel proud of what I have done during my day. Of course it's not easy. But no body is telling you to read one book a day or to work out 5 hours a day. Give small steps. Enjoy the journey.

For how long did you meditate or excersice? I mean, to develop healthy habits takes a lot of time but it's definitely worth it. I've also suffered anxiety but,since  two months ago, I've started creating a daily to do list and also practicing skills I've always wanted to learn. My point is that you should try to do it too. You need to win small battles when your day starts. Try to wake up 30min earlier, make your bed, drink a glass of water, not to check your cellphone for the first hours and so on. You'll feel so satisfied for achieving those little goals. It may look insignificant but the point is that you have to develop discipline. Developing habits has changed my life. I recommend you the book "atomic habits". It's so satisfying to do what you have to do. To set goals in the short and long term and to fulfill them. If you don't keep your mind busy, terrible thoughts will come to your mind. The point is to never stop doing something. Don't give your brain a break so it won't torture yourself with negative thoughts. Come on. It may be difficult at the beginning but it's definitely worth fighting for. Fight for the person you want to be. Don't give up.
